variables.name: hgrids
variables.comment: Grid spacing in the three directions (bohr)
variables.description: Grid spacing in three directions (Bohr units) of the coarse mesh as [0.5, 0.45, 0.4]. A scalar can also be given as 0.45. The grid spacing of the Cartesian grid, in Bohr. As described in the wavelet formalism section, the nodes of this grid serve as the centers for the scaling function/wavelet basis. Values are in most cases between 0.3 and 0.6 bohr.

variables.name: ngrids
variables.comment: Number of grid spacing division in each direction
variables.description: Number of grid spacing division in each direction. Values are relevant only for periodic directions. This is convenient to keep the constant the number of wavelets when changing the super-cell dimensions. These values override hgrid ones.

variables.name: rmult
variables.comment: c(f)rmult*radii_cf(:,1(2))=coarse(fine) atom-based radius
variables.description: Coarse and fine multiplier as [4.0, 8.0]. These numbers determine the extension of the coarse and fine region respectively.

variables.name: ixc
variables.comment: Exchange-correlation parameter (LDA=1,PBE=11)
variables.description: Determine the exchange-correlation functional. Integer specifying which exchange correlation functional will be used. The Abinit conventions are used and detailed information can be found on the Abinit Web page. Here is only a short summary of some widely used functionals - Pade LDA from Abinit XC library; - PBE from Abinit XC library; - Pade LDA from libXC; - PBE from libXC; - PBEsol from libXC; - PBE0 Hybrid functional (local part from libXC). A positive integer refers to a functional from ABINIT library and a negative one from libXC library. In this case, you concatenate the codes for the exchange part and for the correlation part (see the table of codes).

variables.name: qcharge
variables.comment: Charge of the system. Can be integer or real.
variables.description: Total charge of the system. A positive qcharge means that electrons are taken away and a negative one means that extra electrons are added.

variables.name: elecfield
variables.comment: Electric field (Ex,Ey,Ez)
variables.description: Uniform electric field Ex, Ey, Ez in units of Ha/Bohr. The electric field can not have components in periodic directions, e.g. Ex = Ez = 0 in case surface BC is used.

variables.name: nspin
variables.comment: Spin polarization treatment
variables.description: Spin polarization treatment; 1 no spin (as LDA), 2 spin-polarisation (LSD or collinear) and 4 non-collinear i.e. two components per electron.

variables.name: mpol
variables.comment: Total magnetic moment
variables.description: Total magnetic moment which has to be the same parity as the total number of electrons (nelec_up-nelec_down=mpol). You should also define the keyword 'IGSpin' or add a spin per atom to specify the polarisation for the input guess.

variables.name: gnrm_cv
variables.comment: Convergence criterion gradient
variables.description: Convergence criterion for the wavefunction optimization (norm of the gradient). Reasonable values are in most cases between 1.d-4 and 1.d-5.

variables.name: itermax
variables.comment: Max. iterations of wfn. opt. steps
variables.description: Maximum number of gradient evaluations for a single cycle in a wavefunction optimization and maximum number of cycles. At the end of each cycle a subspace diagonalization is done which helps in cases where one has near degeneracy between the HOMO and LUMO orbitals. 50 are usually sufficient.

variables.name: itermin
variables.comment: Minimal iterations of wfn. optimized steps

variables.name: nrepmax
variables.comment: Max. number of re-diag. runs
variables.description: Maximum number of gradient evaluations for a single cycle in a wavefunction optimization and maximum number of cycles. At the end of each cycle a subspace diagonalization is done which helps in cases where one has near degeneracy between the HOMO and LUMO orbitals. 50 are usually sufficient.

variables.name: ncong
variables.comment: No. of CG it. for preconditioning eq.
variables.description: ncong gives the number of iterations in the solution of the preconditioning equation. For free boundary conditions 5 is a good value whereas for other boundary condition a value from 0 to 2 is in general sufficient. Large values of ncong lead to a smaller number of iterations in the wavefunction optimization and better forces, but each iteration is more costly. So an optimal compromise value has to be found.

variables.name: idsx
variables.comment: Wfn. diis history
variables.description: idsx gives the history length of the DIIS convergence acceleration in the wavefunction optimization. 6 is usually a good value for fast convergence. In case of convergence problems it can be advantageous to switch off DIIS by setting idsx = 0. The memory requirements grow considerably with large values of idsx. If memory is the limiting factor one has to choose idsx smaller than the value which gives the fastest convergence. The bigdft-tool tool can be used to predict the memory requirements for different choices of idsx.

variables.name: dispersion
variables.comment: Dispersion correction potential (values 1,2,3,4,5), 0=none
variables.description: A non-zero values activates an empirical add-on treatment of dispersion effects. The values 1, 2 and 3 specify different switching on functions using the convention.

variables.name: inputpsiid
variables.comment: Input guess wavefunctions
variables.description: Specifies how the input guess wavefunction is generated - -2 Random numbers are used as input guess. his is of course a poor input guess which will need many iterations of the wavefunction optimization and might even lead to divergences. - -1 The input wavefunction is imported from the CP2K code which uses Gaussian functions. The basis set should be contained in a file named gaubasis.dat whereas the coefficients should appear in the gaucoeff.dat file. Both files are the output files of CP2K code. See the H2O-CP2K test for an example. - 0 A subspace diagonalization in a minimal atomic basis set is used. This input guess should be used in general if one starts a new calculation. - 1 The previously calculated wavefunctions (for instance from the previous geometry optimization step) are used as input guess. Setting InputPsiId to this value does only make sense from within a main program where call_cluster() subroutine was called previously. The old wavefunction is passed to the new call via the data structure restart. - 2 The input wavefunction is read from the wavefunction. files which contain all the scaling function and wavelet coefficients. In case some parameters such as hgrids or crmult have changed, compared to the previous run, the wavefunctions will be also transformed to the new parameter set. Use also this value to restart from ETSF file format wavefunction-etsf.nc. - 10 The same as 0 but activates the ’Gaussian help’ after convergence the wavefunctions are projected onto the localised basis set used for the input guess, and Mulliken Charge Population Analysis (MCPA) is performed on this basis. The user has the possibility to perform MCPA with separate basis set (functionality to be added). - 11 Restart with Gaussian approximation contained in the ’restart’ data structure. - 12 The input wavefunction is read from the wavefunctions.gau file, which contains an approximation in a minimal Gaussian basis set of the previously calculated wavefunctions. - 100 Use Linear Atomic Orbitals - 101 Restart for Linear - 102 Linear on disk

variables.name: rbuf
variables.comment: Length of the tail (AU)

variables.name: ncongt
variables.comment: No. of tail CG iterations
variables.description: Far reaching tails of the wavefunctions decaying into the vacuum are added in a perturbative treatment if the variable rbuf is set to a strictly positive value. This allows to do a calculation with some moderate value of crmult and then to extrapolate to the limit of large crmult. This procedure is not variational and gives too low energies. The true energy is in between the two energies and in general much closer to the extrapolated energy. This procedure can also be used to judge whether the chosen value of crmult is large enough for a certain required precision. rbuf gives the amount by which the radii for the coarse resolution region are increased in atomic units. ncongt gives the number of iterations used in the perturbation calculation. Reasonable values for ncongt are around 30.

variables.name: norbv
variables.comment: Davidson subspace dimension (No. virtual orbitals)
variables.description: Determine the dimension of the subspace i.e. the number of virtual orbitals to calculate via a Davidson diagonalisation. Usually unoccupied orbitals are not calculated since they are not needed for the total energy and other physical properties of the electronic ground state. Putting norbv to a non-zero value will result in the calculation of norbv virtual orbitals in a postprocessing routine after the occupied orbitals have been calculated, which uses Davidson iterative treatment. nvirt (< norbv) determines to the number of converged orbitals during the convergence process which is taking care of during the Davidson iterations. nplot of these orbitals will be written in the virtual.*.pot files and nplot (if that many exist) of the highest occupied orbitals will be written in the orbital.*.pot file. The Kohn Sham eigenvalues are written in the ordinary output file.

variables.name: nvirt
variables.comment: No. of converged virtual orbs (< norbv)
variables.description: Determine the dimension of the subspace i.e. the number of virtual orbitals to be converged via a Davidson diagonalisation. (should be < norbv) Usually unoccupied orbitals are not calculated since they are not needed for the total energy and other physical properties of the electronic ground state. Putting norbv to a non-zero value will result in the calculation of norbv virtual orbitals in a postprocessing routine after the occupied orbitals have been calculated, which uses Davidson iterative treatment. nvirt (< norbv) determines to the number of converged orbitals during the convergence process which is taking care of during the Davidson iterations. nplot of these orbitals will be written in the virtual.*.pot files and nplot (if that many exist) of the highest occupied orbitals will be written in the orbital.*.pot file. The Kohn Sham eigenvalues are written in the ordinary output file.

variables.name: nplot

variables.description: Number of orbitals to be plotted Determine the dimension of the subspace i.e. the number of virtual orbitals to calculate via a Davidson diagonalisation. Usually unoccupied orbitals are not calculated since they are not needed for the total energy and other physical properties of the electronic ground state. Putting norbv to a non-zero value will result in the calculation of norbv virtual orbitals in a postprocessing routine after the occupied orbitals have been calculated, which uses Davidson iterative treatment . nplot of these orbitals will be written in the virtual.*.pot files and nplot (if that many exist) of the highest occupied orbitals will be written in the orbital.*.pot file The Kohn Sham eigenvalues are written in the ordinary output file. nvirt corresponds to the actual number of orbitals the convergence process is taking care of during the Davidson iterations.

variables.name: frac_fluct
variables.comment: Fraction of force fluctuations. Stop if fmax < forces_fluct*frac_fluct
variables.description: Convergence criteria for the geometry optimization. The geometry optimization stops either if the norm of the individual forces acting on any atom in the system is smaller than forcemax or if the forces get noisy. Noise is present because of the underlying integration grid. The parameter frac_fluct specifies how small the forces should become compared to the noise level to stop the geometry optimization. Values in between 1 and 10 is are reasonable for this parameter. A value of 2 means that the geometry optimization will stop when the largest atomic force is comparable to the 2 times the average noise in the forces themselves. For values of frac_fluct smaller than 1 one can under certain circumstances obtain better relaxed geometries but one risks that the geometry optimization will not converge since the forces are too noisy. In such a case one should closely monitor the progress of the geometry optimization by looking at the posout. files which are written at each step of the geometry optimization and at the data/geopt.mon file.

variables.name: forcemax
variables.comment: Max forces criterion when stop
variables.description: Convergence criteria for the geometry optimization. The geometry optimization stops either if the norm of the individual forces acting on any atom in the system is smaller than forcemax or if the forces get noisy. Noise is present because of the underlying integration grid. The parameter frac_fluct specifies how small the forces should become compared to the noise level to stop the geometry optimization. Values in between 1 and 10 is are reasonable for this parameter. A value of 2 means that the geometry optimization will stop when the largest atomic force is comparable to the 2 times the average noise in the forces themselves. For values of frac_fluct smaller than 1 one can under certain circumstances obtain better relaxed geometries but one risks that the geometry optimization will not converge since the forces are too noisy. In such a case one should closely monitor the progress of the geometry optimization by looking at the posout. files which are written at each step of the geometry optimization and at the data/geopt.mon file.

variables.name: randdis
variables.comment: Random displacement amplitude
variables.description: This parameter allows to add random displacements with amplitude randdis to the atomic positions in the input file posinp. This can for instance be useful to break degeneracies (which would lead to convergence problems in the wavefunction optimization) in highly symmetric structures.

variables.name: betax
variables.comment: Stepsize for the geometry optimization
variables.description: This is the stepsize for the geometry optimization. This stepsize is system dependent and it has therefore to be determined for each system. If the VSSD method is used one can start with a small stepsize of around 1 and VSSD will suggest then a better value for {betax} in the last line of the data/geopt.mon file. Whether the stepsize is correct can also be seen from the data/geopt.mon output of the SDCG method. In this case the average stepsize in terms of betax should be around 4 (after a brief initial period where it is around 8). In contrast to the SDCG method, the BFGS method is not very sensitive to the correct stepsize but nevertheless one should try to find reasonable values also in this case. SQNM: For many systems 1 is a good stepsize. Some systems can be minimized more efficiently with a larger stepsize.

variables.name: adjust_kernel_iterations
variables.comment: Enable the adaptive ajustment of the number of kernel iterations

variables.name: adjust_kernel_threshold
variables.comment: Enable the adaptive ajustment of the kernel convergence threshold according to the support function convergence

variables.name: wf_extent_analysis
variables.comment: Perform an analysis of the extent of the support functions (and possibly KS orbitals)

variables.name: foe_gap
variables.comment: Use the FOE method to calculate the HOMO-LUMO gap at the end of a calculation

variables.name: calculate_forces
variables.comment: Whether or not to calculate the forces at the end of a run (cubic and linear)

variables.name: hybrid
variables.comment: Activate the hybrid mode; if activated, only the low accuracy values will be relevant

variables.name: nit
variables.comment: Number of iteration with low/high accuracy
variables.description: Maximal number of outer loop iterations (high / low accuracy). In each iteration both the support function and the kernel are optimized. When the hybrid mode is used, only the first entry is taken into account.

variables.name: rpnrm_cv
variables.comment: Convergence criterion for low/high accuracy
variables.description: Convergence criterion for the outer loop iterations (high / low accuracy). The optimization stops if the mean change of the charge density / potential falls below this threshold. When the hybrid mode is used, only the first entry is taken into account.

variables.name: conf_damping
variables.comment: How the confinement should be decreased, only relevant for hybrid mode; negative -> automatic
variables.description: Prescription how the prefactor for the confining potential should be decreased * negative value => automatic adjustment (recommended) * positive value => at each iteration the prefactor is multiplied with the specified value This variable is only relevant for the hybrid mode.

variables.name: taylor_order
variables.comment: Order of the Taylor approximation; 0 -> exact
variables.description: Indicates how the matrix powers are calculated: * n<0 => Laura's method of order n * n=0 => exact calculation * n>0 => Taylor series of order n

variables.name: max_inversion_error
variables.comment: Linear scaling maximal error of the Taylor approximations to calculate the inverse of the overlap matrix
variables.description: Maximal error of the Taylor approximations which are used to calculate the inverse of the overlap matrix. If this error is larger than the specified value, the order of the Taylor approximation is increased. The default value is set very large, such such in this case no automatic adjustment is performed.

variables.name: output_wf
variables.comment: Output basis functions; 0 no output, 1 formatted output, 2 Fortran bin, 3 ETSF
variables.description: Indicates how the support functions should be written to disk at the end of the run: * 0 => None * 1 => Wavelet, Plain text * 2 => Wavelet, Fortran binary * 3 => Wavelet, ETSF file format * 10 => None * 11 => Wavelet and Interpolating Scaling Function (density), Plain text * 12 => Wavelet and Interpolating Scaling Function (density), Fortran binary * 13 => Wavelet and Interpolating Scaling Function (density), ETSF file format * 20 => None * 21 => Wavelet and Interpolating Scaling Function (wavefunction), Plain text * 22 => Wavelet and Interpolating Scaling Function (wavefunction), Fortran binary * 23 => Wavelet and Interpolating Scaling Function (wavefunction), ETSF file format

enum.label: Wavelet and Interpolating Scaling Function (density), Plain text
Wavelet and Interpolating Scaling Function (density), Fortran binary
Wavelet and Interpolating Scaling Function (density), ETSF file format
Wavelet and Interpolating Scaling Function (wavefunction), Plain text
Wavelet and Interpolating Scaling Function (wavefunction), Fortran binary
Wavelet and Interpolating Scaling Function (wavefunction), ETSF file format

variables.name: output_mat
variables.comment: Output sparse matrices; 0 no output, 1 formatted sparse, 11 formatted dense, 21 formatted both.
variables.description: Indicates how the support function matrices should be written to disk at the end of the run: * 0 => None * 1 => Plain text in sparse format * 11 => Plain text in dense format * 21 => Plain text in both formats * 2 => Fortran binary in sparse format * 12 => Fortran binary in dense format * 22 => Fortran binary in both formats * 4 => MPI native binary in sparse format

variables.name: output_matder
variables.comment: Output sparse matrices derivatives; 0 no output, 1 formatted sparse,
variables.description: Indicates how the support function matrices should be written to disk at the end of the run: * 0 => None * 1 => Plain text in sparse format

variables.name: output_coeff
variables.comment: Output KS coefficients; 0 no output, 1 formatted output
variables.description: Indicates how the support function coefficients should be written to disk at the end of the run: * 0 => None * 1 => Plain text

variables.name: output_multipole_matrices
variables.comment: If outputting support function matrices, also output the multipole matrices in the same format as the other matrices

variables.name: output_matmul
variables.comment: If outputting support function matrices, also include the matmul file

variables.name: output_fragments
variables.comment: Output support functions, kernel and coeffs; 0 fragments and full system, 1 fragments only, 2 full system only
variables.description: Indicates how the support functions should be written to disk at the end of the run: * 0 => Fragments and full system * 1 => Fragments only * 2 => Full system only

variables.name: kernel_restart_mode
variables.comment: Method for restarting kernel; 0 kernel, 1 coefficients, 2 random, 3 diagonal, 4 full kernel, 5 full coeffs
variables.description: Indicates how the kernel should be generated for a restart calculation: * 0 => Density kernel * 1 => Coefficients * 2 => Random * 3 => Diagonal kernel, i.e. support functions scaled by number of electrons (per fragment) * 4 => Atomic orbitals, i.e. first perform diagonalization and retain coefficients/kernel * 5 => Density kernel of full system (for the case where both fragment and full kernel is available) * 6 => Coefficients of full system (for the case where both fragment and full kernel is available) * 7 => Diagonal kernel with smearing

variables.name: kernel_restart_noise
variables.comment: Add random noise to kernel or coefficients when restarting
variables.description: Indicates how much noise should be added to kernel or coefficients for a restart calculation

variables.name: frag_num_neighbours
variables.comment: Number of neighbours to output for each fragment
variables.description: Indicates how many neighbouring atoms should be written to frag_env.xyz - only allow for a small number of neighbours

variables.name: frag_neighbour_cutoff
variables.comment: Number of neighbours to output for each fragment
variables.description: Distance (in bohr) beyond which neighbouring atoms are not included in frag_env.xyz

variables.name: cdft_add_w_guess
variables.comment: Add cdft_add_w_guess * W to kernel for CDFT initial guess
variables.description: possible value: 1 real number

variables.name: calc_dipole
variables.comment: Calculate dipole
variables.description: Indicates whether the dipole moment should be calculated after the run or not

variables.name: calc_quadrupole
variables.comment: Calculate quadrupole
variables.description: Indicates whether the quadrupole moment should be calculated after the run or not

variables.name: subspace_diag
variables.comment: Diagonalization at the end
variables.description: Indicates whether a diagonalization shall be performed at the end of the run

variables.name: extra_states
variables.comment: Number of extra states to include in support function and kernel optimization (dmin only), must be equal to norbsempty

variables.name: calculate_onsite_overlap
variables.comment: Calculate the onsite overlap matrix (has only an effect if the matrices are all written to disk)

variables.name: charge_multipoles
variables.comment: Calculate the atom-centered multipole coefficients; 0 no, 1 old approach Loewdin, 2 new approach Projector
variables.description: Calculate the multipole expansion coefficients of the atomic charge which can then be used to establish a QM/MM coupling. Currently only implemented and tested for nspin=1 Possible values are: * 0 => no calculation * 1 => Loewdin approach, however without explicit orthogonalization #* 2 => new approach using simple projector and orthogonalized support functions #* 3 => new approach using full projector and orthogonalized support functions * 11 => Mulliken approach #* 12 => same as 2, but with non-orthogonalized support functions #* 13 => same as 3, but with non-orthogonalized support functions

enum.label: Loewdin approach, however without explicit orthogonalization

variables.name: check_multipoles
variables.comment: Check the multipoles computed by computing the total dipole.

variables.name: support_function_multipoles
variables.comment: Calculate the multipole moments of the support functions

variables.name: plot_locreg_grids
variables.comment: Plot the scaling function and wavelets grid of each localization region

variables.name: calculate_FOE_eigenvalues
variables.comment: First and last eigenvalue to be calculated using the FOE procedure

variables.name: precision_FOE_eigenvalues
variables.comment: Decay length of the error function used to extract the eigenvalues (i.e. something like the resolution)

variables.name: multipole_centers
variables.comment: Determines whether the multipole centers shall be determined automatically (i.e. taking the atoms) or whether they are provided manually

variables.name: consider_entropy
variables.comment: Indicate whether the entropy contribution to the total energy shall be considered

variables.name: nit
variables.comment: Maximal number of iterations in the optimization of the support functions
variables.description: Maximal number of iterations in the optimization of the support functions. The first number is used for the low accuracy part, the second one for the high accuracy part. If the hybrid mode is used, only the first value is taken into account.

variables.name: nit_ig
variables.comment: maximal number of iterations to optimize the support functions in the extended input guess (experimental mode only)

variables.name: extended_ig
variables.comment: whether or not to do an extended input guess (will be activated by default in experimental mode)

variables.name: orthogonalize_sfs
variables.comment: whether or not to explicitly orthogonalize SFs (will be activated by default except in experimental mode, and may eventually be automatically turned off)

variables.name: idsx
variables.comment: DIIS history for optimization of the support functions (low/high accuracy); 0 -> SD
variables.description: Indicates the method with which the support functions are optimized * n=0 => steepest descent * n>0 => DIIS with history length n

variables.name: gnrm_cv
variables.comment: Convergence criterion for the optimization of the support functions (low/high accuracy)
variables.description: Convergence criterion for optimization of the support functions (high / low accuracy). The optimization stops if the mean gradient norm falls below this threshold. When the hybrid mode is used, only the first entry is taken into account.

variables.name: gnrm_ig
variables.comment: Convergence criterion for the optimization of the support functions in the extended input guess (experimental mode only)

variables.name: deltae_cv
variables.comment: Total relative energy difference to stop the optimization ('experimental_mode' only)
variables.description: The optimization of the support functions stops if the total relative gain in the target function during the given cycle of support function optimization falls below this threshold

variables.name: gnrm_dyn
variables.comment: Dynamic convergence criterion ('experimental_mode' only)
variables.description: From this value the effective dynamic convergence criterion is calculated by a division by kappa. Then the optimization of the support functions stops if the mean gradient norm falls below this effective dynamic convergence criterion and is at the same time smaller than the value of min_gnrm_for_dynamic. The specified value should be approximately 10 times smaller than the value of gnrm_cv. This value is only used for the experimental mode.

variables.name: min_gnrm_for_dynamic
variables.comment: Minimal gnrm to active the dynamic gnrm criterion
variables.description: The dynamic convergence criterion (specified by gnrm_dyn) is only active if the mean gradient norm of the support functions is below this threshold

variables.name: alpha_diis
variables.comment: Multiplicator for DIIS
variables.description: possible value: 2 positive real numbers The support functions gradient is multiplied by this number before being used for the DIIS optimization. The first entry for the low accuracy part, the second one for the high accuracy part. When the hybrid mode is used, only the first entry is taken into account.

variables.name: alpha_sd
variables.comment: Initial step size for SD
variables.description: The initial step size which is used to optimize the support functions with steepest descent. If the specified value is not appropriate, it will be adjusted automatically. The first entry is used for the low accuracy part, the second one for the high accuracy part. When the hybrid mode is used, only the first entry is taken into account.

variables.name: nstep_prec
variables.comment: Number of iterations in the preconditioner
variables.description: Indicates how many iterations in the preconditioning of the gradient shall be performed

variables.name: fix_basis
variables.comment: Fix the support functions if the density change is below this threshold

variables.name: correction_orthoconstraint
variables.comment: Correction for the slight non-orthonormality in the orthoconstraint
variables.description: Indicates whether the slight non-orthogonality of the support functions should be taken into account during the application of the orthogonality constraint - 0 => take into account - 1 => don't take into account

variables.name: orthogonalize_ao
variables.comment: Orthogonalize the atomic orbitals used as input guess

variables.name: reset_DIIS_history
variables.comment: Reset the DIIS history when starting the loop which optimizes the support functions

variables.name: nstep
variables.comment: Number of steps taken when updating the coefficients via direct minimization for each iteration of the density kernel loop
variables.description: Indicates the number of steps taken when updating the coefficients via direct minimization for each iteration of the density kernel loop. The first entry is used for the low accuracy part, the second one for the high accuracy part. When the hybrid mode is used, only the first entry is taken into account.

variables.name: nit
variables.comment: Number of iterations in the (self-consistent) optimization of the density kernel
variables.description: Indicates the number of iterations in the (self-consistent) optimization of the density kernel. The first entry is used for the low accuracy part, the second one for the high accuracy part. When the hybrid mode is used, only the first entry is taken into account.

variables.name: idsx_coeff
variables.comment: DIIS history for direct mininimization - warning, there is currently a problem for idsx_coeff/=0

variables.name: idsx
variables.comment: Mixing method; 0 -> linear mixing, >=1 -> Pulay mixing
variables.description: Indicates how the density / potential mixing shall be performed: n=0 => linear mixing n=1 => Pulay mixing with history length n The first entry is used for the low accuracy part, the second one for the high accuracy part. When the hybrid mode is used, only the first entry is taken into account.

variables.name: alphamix
variables.comment: Mixing parameter (low/high accuracy)
variables.description: Indicates the mixing parameter used for the mixing of the charge density / potential. The larger the value, the more of the previous value will be kept. The first entry is used for the low accuracy part, the second one for the high accuracy part. When the hybrid mode is used, only the first entry is taken into account.

variables.name: gnrm_cv_coeff
variables.comment: Convergence criterion on the gradient for direct minimization
variables.description: Convergence criterion on the gradient for direct minimization. The first entry is used for the low accuracy part, the second one for the high accuracy part. When the hybrid mode is used, only the first entry is taken into account.

variables.name: rpnrm_cv
variables.comment: Convergence criterion (change in density/potential) for the kernel optimization
variables.description: The optimization of the density kernel is stopped as soon as the mean change of the charge density / potential between two iterations falls below this threshold. The first entry is used for the low accuracy part, the second one for the high accuracy part. When the hybrid mode is used, only the first entry is taken into account.

variables.name: linear_method
variables.comment: Method to optimize the density kernel
variables.description: Indicates the method with which the density kernel is optimized: * DIRMIN => direct minimization * DIAG => diagonalization with density mixing * NTPOLY => diagonalization using NTPoly. * FOE => Fermi Operator Expansion

variables.name: mixing_method
variables.comment: Quantity to be mixed
variables.description: Indicates which quantity should be used for the mixing procedure: DEN => density mixing POT => potential mixing

variables.name: alpha_sd_coeff
variables.comment: Initial step size for SD for direct minimization

variables.name: alpha_fit_coeff
variables.comment: Update the SD step size by fitting a quadratic polynomial
variables.description: Update the SD step size by fitting a quadratic polynomial to the energy along the direction of the gradient during direct mininimization.

variables.name: coeff_scaling_factor
variables.comment: Factor to scale the gradient in direct minimization
variables.description: Specifies a scaling factor for the coefficient gradient, recommended to be around 0.1 - 0.5 for CDFT, fragment calculations or systems where convergence is unstable.

variables.name: delta_pnrm
variables.comment: Stop the kernel optimization if the density/potential difference has decreased by this factor (deactivated if -1.0)
variables.description: stop the kernel optimization if the density/potential difference has decreased by this factor compared to the first iteration. The feature is deactivated for a value of -1.0

variables.name: diag_start
variables.comment: whether or not to diagonalize the SF Hamiltonian at the beginning of a restart calculation (useful for (pseudo-)fragment calculations)

variables.name: nbasis
variables.comment: Number of support functions per atom
variables.description: Indicates the number of support fuctions centered on this atom type. Possible values are: * 1 (s orbital type) * 4 (s,p orbital types) * 9 (s,p,d orbital types) * 16 (s,p,d,f orbital types)

variables.name: ao_confinement
variables.comment: Prefactor for the input guess confining potential
variables.description: Indicates the prefactor of the confining potential of this atom type which is used to generate the input guess.

variables.name: confinement
variables.comment: Prefactor for the confining potential (low/high accuracy)
variables.description: Indicates the prefactor of the confining potential of this atom type. The first entry is used for the low accuracy part, the second one for the high accuracy part. When the hybrid mode is used, only the first entry is taken into account.

variables.name: rloc
variables.comment: Localization radius for the support functions
variables.description: Indicates the cutoff radius for the support functions. The first entry is used for the low accuracy part, the second one for the high accuracy part; the second value must not be smaller than the first one. When the hybrid mode is used, only the first entry is taken into account.

variables.name: rloc_kernel
variables.comment: Localization radius for the density kernel
variables.description: Indicates the cutoff radius for the density kernel. Must be at least as large as the support function cutoff plus 8 times the grid spacing; will be adjusted automatically if it is chosen too small.

variables.name: rloc_kernel_foe
variables.comment: Cutoff radius for the FOE matrix vector multiplications
variables.description: Indicates the cutoff radius used for the matrix vector multiplications. Must be at least as large as the kernel cutoff.

linear_accurate.comment: Appropriate input parameters for a high accuracy linear scaling calculation
linear_accurate.description: This profile should be chosen if highly accurate energy differences are required.

linear_moderate.comment: Appropriate input parameters for a moderate accuracy linear scaling calculation
linear_moderate.description: This profile should be chosen if accurate forces are required, but there is no need for extremely accurate energies.

linear_fast.comment: Appropriate input parameters for a low accuracy linear scaling calculation
linear_fast.description: This profile should be chosen if speed is more important than accuracy.

mixing.comment: To be used for metallic systems
mixing.description: Parameters for the mixing scheme associated to the diagonalization method.

linear.comment: Linear parameters sufficient for PDoS, charge analysis, MD
linear.description: Basic parameters to perform a linear calculation.

linear_virtual.comment: Input parameters to be added to the linear profile for virtual states inclusion

linear_fragments.comment: Input parameters to be added to the linear profile for fragment calculation (templates ready)

linear_convergence.comment: Parameters to supplement linear to help with convergence.
linear_convergence.description: Include this profile with linear if you have convergence problems.

linear_purify.comment: Input parameters to turn on purification instead of chess
linear_purify.description: Extra parameters for linear if you want to use NTPoly purification

md.comment: Molecular dynamics input parameters for H2O molecules

variables.name: screening
variables.comment: Mu screening parameter
variables.description: Activates the exponential (Yukawa-like) screening in the coulomb kernel

variables.name: isf_order
variables.comment: Order of the Interpolating Scaling Function family
variables.description: Fixes the order of the ISF family that is used for the discretization of the kernel

variables.name: stress_tensor
variables.comment: Triggers the calculation of the stress tensor
variables.description: It calculates the derivative of the hartree energy with respect to the deformation. It makes sense only for a vacuum-like calculation

variables.name: evboundsshrink_nsatur
variables.comment: Maximal number of unsuccessful eigenvalue bounds shrinkings

variables.name: fscale
variables.comment: Initial guess for the error function decay length
variables.description: Indicates the decay length of the error function which is used by the Fermi Operator Expasion to construct the density kernel. This value will be adjusted automatically if not chosen appropriately.

variables.name: fscale_lowerbound
variables.comment: Lower bound for the error function decay length

variables.name: fscale_upperbound
variables.comment: Upper bound for the error function decay length

variables.name: eval_range_foe
variables.comment: Lower and upper bound of the eigenvalue spectrum, will be adjusted automatically if chosen unproperly
variables.description: Indicates the lower and upper bound of the eigenvalue spectrum which is used for the Fermi Operator Expansion. This spectrum will be adjusted automatically if not chosen appropriately.

variables.name: accuracy_foe
variables.comment: Required accuracy for the Chebyshev fit for FOE

variables.name: accuracy_ice
variables.comment: Required accuracy for the Chebyshev fit for ICE (calculation of matrix powers)

variables.name: accuracy_penalty
variables.comment: Required accuracy for the Chebyshev fit for the penalty function

variables.name: accuracy_entropy
variables.comment: Required accuracy for the Chebyshev fit for the function to calculate the entropy term

variables.name: betax_foe
variables.comment: the exponent in the exponential penalty function which is used to determine the eigenvalue bounds for FOE

variables.name: betax_ice
variables.comment: the exponent in the exponential penalty function which is used to determine the eigenvalue bounds for ICE

variables.name: occupation_function
variables.comment: the function to assign the occupation numbers

variables.name: adjust_fscale
variables.comment: dynamically adjust the value of fscale or not

variables.name: matmul_optimize_load_balancing
variables.comment: optimize the load balancing of the sparse matrix matrix multiplications (at the cost of memory unbalancing)

variables.name: fscale_ediff_low
variables.comment: lower bound for the optimal relative energy difference between the kernel and the control kernel

variables.name: fscale_ediff_up
variables.comment: upper bound for the optimal relative energy difference between the kernel and the control kernel

variables.comment: turn on serial IO if MPI is having problem on a machine.

variables.comment: threshold for flushing small matrix values of the density matrix.

variables.name: convergence_density
variables.comment: threshold for convergence of ntpoly purification calculation.

variables.name: threshold_overlap
variables.comment: threshold for flushing small matrix values of the overlap matrix.

variables.name: convergence_overlap
variables.comment: threshold for convergence of ntpoly overlap inverse calculation.

variables.name: temperature
variables.comment: temperature in Kelvin for smearing.

variables.name: step_size
variables.comment: step size for differential equation solvers (WOM)

variables.name: solver
variables.comment: the density matrix solver to use.
